h1: Coco View Hotel — a city hotel in Maeklong town with a salt-water pool and gym all in one place
intro: If you want to stay in Maeklong town itself — easy reach to the umbrella market, the Mae Klong floating market and Amphawa — but still want a pool and proper hotel-style rooms rather than a canalside wooden house, Coco View Hotel is a name self-drive visitors keep coming back to. It's a 3-star hotel of around 40 rooms in Mae Klong sub-district, Mueang district, set beside a canal. What guests mention most is the salt-water swimming pool, a gym that reviews call better than expected, a varied breakfast and roomy, clean rooms. Standard rooms start at about THB 1,200/night, rising on weekends and holidays.

body.html: Most stays around Samut Songkhram are wooden shophouses or homestays along the Amphawa canal. Coco View Hotel instead sits in Maeklong town itself, in Mae Klong sub-district, Mueang district, beside a small canal, which buys you city-hotel convenience and quick access to all the main sights. It opened around 2014–2015 with roughly 40 rooms in a building that still looks modern — a fit for travellers who want full facilities rather than a vintage wooden-house atmosphere.

What guests talk about most is the outdoor salt-water swimming pool and a gym that many reviews call better than expected for a hotel this size — a few even say it's the best hotel gym they've come across in a provincial town. There's a sauna, plus the Coco Kitchen restaurant serving Thai, Chinese and Western food, with a breakfast praised as varied and decent. Free Wi-Fi, free parking and a 24-hour front desk round it out — features self-drive visitors appreciate, since most canalside stays in this area don't have them.

"Spacious room, comfy bed, the salt-water pool was clean and the gym was great. Breakfast had plenty to choose from, the staff were attentive and even gave us welcome coconut juice — a good place for families."

Rooms range from Superior Twin and Deluxe to Junior Suite and Coco View Suite. Every room has air-conditioning, a fridge, minibar, flat-screen TV, coffee machine and an en-suite bathroom with hot water; some have a balcony with city or canal views. Many guests say the rooms are spacious, the beds comfortable and everything clean. Worth knowing: some reviews note that furniture and bathroom fittings in a few rooms are starting to show their age, and the soundproofing between rooms isn't thick, so you may hear the next room or the hallway.

On location, the hotel is in Maeklong town, about 5–10 minutes' drive to the umbrella market and the Mae Klong floating market. Amphawa floating market is around 10–15 minutes away, and the Don Hoi Lot viewpoint about 15–20 minutes. The upside is being close to every main sight without long drives, with restaurants and convenience stores all around. The trade-off is that the hotel is near the road and an elevated highway, so some rooms catch traffic noise — if you're sensitive to sound, ask for an inner-facing or higher-floor room.

Honestly, from the real-guest reviews — Coco View Hotel suits travellers who want a city hotel with a pool and gym to use as a base for the umbrella market, Maeklong and Amphawa, more than those after a wooden-house, canalside Amphawa feel. Its clear strengths are the salt-water pool, the gym, the breakfast, roomy units and the convenient in-town location. What you accept in return is noise from neighbouring rooms and the road, and some rooms with older fittings. The cross-platform average sits around 8.0 out of 10 (Trip.com about 7.9, Hotels.com as high as 9.0, Tripadvisor 3.6 out of 5) — a good-value city hotel at this price.

A tip from following the reviews here: ask for a higher floor or an inner-facing room away from the road to dodge traffic and hallway noise. Make the most of the salt-water pool and gym, since they're a real edge over other stays in this area. And if you're heading to the umbrella market, check the train timetable first — the highlight is the moment the awnings fold back as the train passes through.

honestSummary: Coco View Hotel is a city hotel in Maeklong town with a salt-water pool, gym and proper hotel-style rooms at an accessible price — its strengths are full facilities, a location near the umbrella market, Maeklong and Amphawa, and a varied breakfast. It doesn't offer the wooden-house, canalside Amphawa atmosphere, and there's some noise from neighbouring rooms and the road, but if you want a city hotel to use as a convenient base, it works well.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Coco View Hotel, Samut Songkhram

faq.q: Where is Coco View Hotel, and how close is the umbrella market?
faq.a: The hotel is at 144 Samut Songkhram-Bang Phae Road, Mae Klong sub-district, Mueang Samut Songkhram, in Maeklong town beside a canal. It's about 5–10 minutes' drive to the umbrella (Maeklong railway) market and the Mae Klong floating market, 10–15 minutes to Amphawa floating market, and 15–20 minutes to Don Hoi Lot. Free parking is available.

faq.q: What does Coco View Hotel cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Standard rooms start at about THB 1,200/night for a Superior Twin. There are also Deluxe Rooms, Junior Suites and the larger Coco View Suite for families. Prices rise on weekends and holidays — always compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does it have a pool and gym?
faq.a: Yes to both. There's an outdoor salt-water swimming pool, a gym and a sauna. The gym is praised in several reviews as better than expected for a hotel this size — a real advantage, since most canalside stays in this area have neither a pool nor a gym.

faq.q: Is it good for families or couples?
faq.a: It suits both. There are Junior Suites and a Coco View Suite that are roomy for families, plus twin and double rooms for couples. With a pool for kids, a varied breakfast and an in-town location with easy access to the sights, it works well for travellers using the hotel as a base.

faq.q: What are the reviews like, and what should I know?
faq.a: The cross-platform average is around 8.0 out of 10 (Trip.com about 7.9, Hotels.com as high as 9.0, Tripadvisor 3.6 out of 5). Praise centres on the salt-water pool, the gym, the breakfast, roomy units and the in-town location. Things to know: soundproofing between rooms is thin, the hotel is near a road and elevated highway so some rooms catch traffic noise, and furniture in a few rooms is dated.
